thesis_summary.thesis: Lowe's Companies, Inc. (LOW) is the second-largest home improvement retailer in the United States, operating **1,759** stores and outlets with roughly **196 million** square feet of selling space as of January 30, 2026. **[Fact]** The company also operates **540+** wholesale branch locations in the U.S. and Canada after acquiring Foundation Building Materials (FBM) and Artisan Design Group (ADG) in fiscal 2025. **[Fact]** FY2025 net sales were **$86.3 billion** (+3.1% versus $83.7 billion in fiscal 2024), with comparable sales up **0.2%** (average ticket +3.0%, transactions -2.8%). **[Fact]** FY2025 free cash flow was **$7.7 billion** ($9.9 billion operating cash flow minus $2.2 billion capital spending) on **560 million** diluted shares, or about **$13.66** per share. Lowe's serves DIY homeowners and professional (Pro) contractors through big-box stores, e-commerce, installation services, and wholesale distribution.
thesis_summary.why_market_wrong: There is **no dated mispricing catalyst** (HK predictive attribute: **none**). **[Inference]** The market may treat Lowe's as a pure housing-cycle play and underweight the Pro customer strategy, wholesale acquisitions, and durable cash generation through ticket inflation and supply-chain scale. **[Fact]** FY2025 net sales grew **3.1%** despite flat comps, driven by FBM/ADG acquisitions adding **$2.2 billion** in Other segment revenue. **[Fact]** Share repurchases fell to **$211 million** (from **$4.1 billion** in FY2024) while long-term debt rose to **$37.5 billion**, signaling a capital-allocation pivot toward Pro distribution. **[Inference]** Generalists anchoring on GAAP net income decline (**$6.7 billion** versus **$7.0 billion** prior year) may miss that owner cash remained strong at **$7.7 billion** of free cash flow. The inefficiency is **descriptive** (quality compounder at a full price), not a timed equity yield-curve setup.
